title: LC Oscillators and VCOs
intro: An LC tank resonates at 1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)) but loses energy in its resistance. An amplifier supplies negative resistance to compensate.

blocks.alt: An LC tank circuit: an inductor L, a fixed capacitor and a variable capacitor (varactor) all connected in parallel between a top and bottom rail. An arrow through the varactor shows that its value is set by the tuning voltage.
blocks.caption: An LC tank with a varactor. The tuning voltage changes the capacitance, and with it the resonant frequency.

blocks.source:
f0 = 1 / (2*pi*sqrt(L*C))       Q = R_p / (w0*L)  (parallel loss R_p)
Sustained oscillation needs  gm >= 1/R_p

items: Cross-coupled pair: provides the negative resistance -2/gm to cancel R_p.
Phase noise falls with higher tank Q and larger signal swing.
A varactor (voltage-dependent capacitor) in the tank tunes the frequency: this is an LC VCO.

blocks.text: A VCO has an output frequency w_out = w0 + K_VCO * V_cont, so its output phase is the integral of the control voltage. This integration is why a VCO appears as 1/s in a PLL loop.

blocks.title: LC frequency
blocks.text: L = 1 nH and C = 1 pF. Find the resonant frequency.

blocks.text: f0 = 2 GHz at Vcont = 0, K_VCO = 500 MHz/V. What is the output at Vcont = 0.8 V?
